note: Reverse Proxy Header has NO UI, config entity, permissions, Drush or plugins. It is configured ONLY through $settings in settings.php: $settings['reverse_proxy_header'] (the $_SERVER header key holding the real client IP) and $settings['reverse_proxy_header_trusted_addresses_ignore'] (bool). A KernelEvents::REQUEST subscriber at priority 350 reads that header, takes the first FILTER_VALIDATE_IP value and writes REMOTE_ADDR. Settings are read fresh on every Drupal bootstrap, so `drush ev "print Settings::get('reverse_proxy_header');"` reflects settings.php. Medium/hard cases write a marker-guarded block (// >>> rph-eval >>> ... // <<< rph-eval <<<) into web/sites/default/settings.php and read it back via Settings::get; cleanup/reset strip that block and any reverse_proxy_header assignment so the site is left clean. Header names are namespaced HTTP_X_RPH_*.

evals.prompt: The real client IP reaches my Drupal 11 site in a custom header named HTTP_X_REAL_CLIENT_IP that I cannot rename on the proxy. Using the reverse_proxy_header module, how and where do I tell Drupal to use that header for the client IP? Is there an admin settings page?
evals.expected_output: There is no admin UI/config. In settings.php set $settings['reverse_proxy_header'] = 'HTTP_X_REAL_CLIENT_IP'; the module's request subscriber then reads that header and restores the client IP into REMOTE_ADDR.

evals.prompt: With the reverse_proxy_header module, how do I control whether the custom client-IP header is trusted only from configured trusted proxies versus always trusted? Which setting relaxes that, and what is the security trade-off?
evals.expected_output: By default (flag FALSE) with core $settings['reverse_proxy'] + $settings['reverse_proxy_addresses'] set, the header is trusted only from trusted proxies. Setting $settings['reverse_proxy_header_trusted_addresses_ignore'] = TRUE makes it always use the header value, which risks IP spoofing.

evals.prompt: How does the reverse_proxy_header module choose the client IP from the configured header, and how early does it run in the request so authentication and flood control see the corrected IP?
evals.expected_output: It splits the header on commas and uses the first value passing FILTER_VALIDATE_IP, writing it to REMOTE_ADDR (and calling overrideGlobals). The subscriber runs on KernelEvents::REQUEST at priority 350, before RouterListener/AuthenticationSubscriber.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, reverse_proxy_header is configured to read the real client IP from a specific HTTP header. Inspect the live site's settings and state the exact header name it is configured to use.

On this site reverse_proxy_header is configured. Inspect the live settings and say whether the site is set to trust the custom client-IP header even when the request does not come from a trusted proxy, and which setting determines that.
evals.expected_output: Yes — $settings['reverse_proxy_header_trusted_addresses_ignore'] is TRUE, so the header is always trusted regardless of trusted-proxy checks (the header itself is HTTP_X_RPH_IGNORE_HEADER).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure the reverse_proxy_header module so Drupal reads the real client IP from the HTTP header HTTP_X_RPH_TASK_HEADER. Apply the change so it is live (readable via Settings).
evals.expected_output: settings.php now sets $settings['reverse_proxy_header'] = 'HTTP_X_RPH_TASK_HEADER'; so \Drupal\Core\Site\Settings::get('reverse_proxy_header') returns that value.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure reverse_proxy_header so the real client IP is read from the header HTTP_X_RPH_TASK2 AND the header value is always trusted even when the request is not from a trusted proxy. Apply both required settings to the live site.
evals.expected_output: settings.php sets $settings['reverse_proxy_header'] = 'HTTP_X_RPH_TASK2'; and $settings['reverse_proxy_header_trusted_addresses_ignore'] = TRUE; so Settings::get returns 'HTTP_X_RPH_TASK2' and the ignore flag is TRUE.
